summary.text: Furrion Chill rooftop air conditioners (Lippert) run on 115 V, 60 Hz and are controlled by a Furrion wall thermostat such as the Single Zone Premium FACW12PA-BL. The thermostat LCD shows the room temperature or, when the system detects a fault, an error code (E1-E5 or lo) and the system shuts down.

models.text: Chill rooftop manual CCD-0005592 covers FACR13SA, FACR14SA and FACR15SA (-PS or -BL), ADBs FACT12LA and FACT12SA, and wall thermostats FACW12SA-BL, FACW12PA-BL and FACW12ZA-BL sold separately.
Chill Cube Ducted Variable Speed models: FACR15HEDA, FACR18VSDA, FACR18HEDA and FACR15VSDA (-PS white or -BL black hood), with ADB FACT18VSDA-PS or FACT18VSDA2-PS; R32 refrigerant.
Chill 2/8K/Low Profile with electronic control: FACR13HESA2, FACR15HESA2, FACR08HESA2, FACR13LPSA2, FACR15LPSA2; ADB FACT12CA2-PS; single-zone control box FACC10ESSA2-BL; R32.
Heat Pump Single Zone Wall Thermostat FACW12ESPA-BL (Lippert PN 2023136653) operates a heat-pump rooftop unit and must be connected with control box FACC12ESPA-BL.
Chill Cube (Ducted) Single Zone Wall Thermostat FACW13VSDSA-BL (Lippert PN 2024031600) is compatible with FACC13VSD.

display.text: FACW12PA-BL LCD shows the operation mode, fan speed, and the room temperature or an error code in the same position.
FACW12ESPA-BL heat mode shows F (furnace, if available) or HP (heat pump); F may not appear without a gas furnace, and both cannot run at the same time.
FACW13VSDSA-BL: heat sources enabled by the rear DIP switches appear as F (gas furnace), P (heat pump) or S (heat strip); only one heating device runs at a time.
Chill Cube unit panel has GEAR, mode, fan speed, sleep and filter indicator LEDs; the filter LED lights after 250 hours of operation.
Chill Cube in Load Shed mode: the compressor is on standby and the ADB display flashes LS momentarily and on any input.

reset.text: FACW12PA-BL: press and hold the power button 3 seconds to turn the thermostat on or off.
After a power interruption, the system restarts automatically with the last status and set-points once power is restored.
Enhanced multi-zone thermostat E3: the system shuts down and needs a main power reset; after cycling power, press the power button and reselect the mode.
Chill Cube filter LED: turn the unit off, clean and reinstall the filter, then press and hold SLEEP for 2 seconds to turn the LED off.

checks.text: Unit does not switch on: check that supply voltage is connected, then check the power-supply fuse or circuit protector.
Not cooling enough: set the unit to cooling, select a lower temperature, and clear leaves and dirt from the ventilation grilles.
Abnormal shutdown: the freeze sensor has tripped because the outside temperature is too low or all air nozzles are closed.
FACW12PA-BL: allow about three minutes; the compressor delay runs after a mode is selected or a power event to equalize pressure.
FACW13VSDSA-BL E3: the manual's check is the 120 VAC supply or loose wiring connections with the air conditioner system.
Clean the return filter every four weeks or more in use with warm soapy water, dry it completely, and replace it at least every 12 months (Lippert part 2024049532).
Chill Cube operating range: cooling at 64-109 F outdoor and 60-90 F indoor; heating at 41-75 F outdoor; room humidity under 80%.

parts.text: FACW12ESPA-BL codes name the control-box and thermostat indoor sensors, evaporator sensor, outdoor coil sensor, outdoor ambient sensor and the thermostat-to-control-box link; lo means the +12 V supply is too low.
During installation the freeze sensor is stuck into the center bottom of the evaporator and held by a clamp inserted between the fins.
Troubleshooting names the evaporator fan, condenser fan, blower and seals as service parts, with refrigerant leakage as an abnormal-shutdown cause.
Zone, furnace, heat pump, electric heat and analog/digital DIP switches sit on the control box PCB; single-zone boxes ship with Furnace on.

callTech.text: Low voltage, refrigerant leakage, a damaged evaporator or condenser fan, a defective blower or damaged seals: contact an authorized service agent or Furrion.
Only qualified personnel or a certified service technician may repair the air conditioner; any refrigerant work, including recharging, needs a certified technician (flammable R32).
Never use ignition sources such as a halide torch to search for refrigerant leaks; if a leak is suspected, put out all naked flames.
Only a qualified electrician should connect the rooftop unit to power; a damaged supply cord must be replaced by the manufacturer, service agent or similarly qualified person.
DANGER: DIP switches are set only with all 115 VAC and 12 VDC removed from the control board; if 12 V is present, power must be cycled for the change to take effect.
